{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "Create a static website for a nature-inspired personal blog + small eco restaurant concept called "Moss & Hearth". It should feel like an environmental food diary where the owner writes about seasonal cooking, forest walks, zero-waste kitchen habits, and also presents the restaurant menu. Important: this is only a front-end static site, no backend, no database, no login, no online ordering, no real reservation system. Use mock/sample content only.

Overall direction:
- Style: calm nature theme, earthy green, moss, cream, clay, warm wood colors
- Scenario: personal blog mixed with restaurant website
- Domain: environment, sustainable dining, local produce, low-waste lifestyle
- Visual reference: Netflix style layout inspiration only, like a strong cinematic hero section and horizontal content rows/cards, but adapted for a peaceful restaurant/blog site, not a streaming app
- Tech: simple clean UI, easy to read, responsive, static render
- Interaction: lazy-loading for images/cards/sections so the page feels smooth when scrolling

Pages / Sections required:

1. Home Page
- Full-width cinematic hero banner with nature restaurant photo placeholder
- Big headline: "Seasonal Food, Forest Notes, and Slow Living"
- Short intro paragraph about the owner-chef and eco-friendly kitchen
- Two CTA buttons: "Explore Menu" and "Read Journal"
- Netflix-inspired horizontal rows such as:
  - Featured Seasonal Plates
  - Latest Journal Entries
  - Foraged Ingredients This Month
  - Customer Favorites
- Use large image cards with overlay titles and short descriptions
- Add a subtle dark gradient overlay on hero image
- Include lazy loading behavior for all images

2. About / Story Section
- Personal blog style story of the chef-owner
- Include sections: "Why I Cook This Way", "Our Local Farmers", "Low Waste Promise"
- Add a simple timeline of milestones, for example:
  - 2019: Started documenting wild herb recipes
  - 2021: Opened weekend supper table
  - 2024: Built a small seasonal cafe garden
  - 2026: Expanded the blog into a restaurant journal
- Use static text only

3. Restaurant Menu Page or Section
- Create a beautiful static menu with categories:
  - Forest Breakfast
  - Garden Lunch
  - Hearth Dinner
  - Herbal Drinks
  - Seasonal Desserts
- Each menu item should have name, short description, dietary tag, and price
- Example items can be invented: nettle sourdough toast, roasted carrot barley bowl, mushroom thyme stew, elderflower mint cooler, apple oat crumble
- Add tags like Vegan, Gluten Free, Local, Seasonal
- No cart, no ordering, no payment, no checkout
- Add note: "Menu changes weekly based on harvest and availability"

4. Blog / Journal Section
- Static cards for at least 9 blog posts
- Categories: Recipes, Garden Notes, Sustainability, Foraging, Restaurant Life
- Each card should show image placeholder, title, date, category, 2-line excerpt, and read time
- Include a featured blog post layout at the top
- Clicking can open static detail layout or just anchor/placeholder detail sections, but no CMS
- Use sample content

5. Featured Article Detail Layout
- Create one detailed static article page/section titled "A Week of Cooking With What the Garden Gives"
- Include author name, date, reading time, hero image, article body, pull quote, related posts
- Keep it editorial and clean
- Add paragraph sections about compost, seasonal herbs, imperfect vegetables, and mindful eating

6. Gallery Section
- Create a Netflix-like horizontal scroll gallery with nature/restaurant cards
- Categories:
  - Garden Corners
  - Kitchen Moments
  - Seasonal Plates
  - Forest Walks
- Images should lazy load
- Add hover effect: image zoom, soft shadow, title overlay
- Use static local placeholder image paths or gradients if real images are not available

7. Sustainability Page / Section
- Clear blocks explaining:
  - Composting system
  - Reusable packaging
  - Local sourcing
  - Plant-forward menu
  - Rainwater garden
  - Food waste reduction
- Add simple stat cards with mock values, for example:
  - 82% ingredients sourced within 40 miles
  - 35kg composted weekly
  - 12 local growers featured
- Make sure these are presented as sample/static values

8. Visit / Contact Section
- Restaurant address placeholder
- Opening hours table
- Static contact details
- Simple decorative contact form is okay but it must not submit anywhere; show it as visual-only with disabled/static behavior or a fake success message handled in front-end only
- Include note: "For demo only - no messages are actually sent"
- Add map placeholder image/card, not a real map API

9. Design Requirements
- Responsive desktop/tablet/mobile
- Sticky transparent header that becomes solid on scroll
- Navigation links: Home, Story, Menu, Journal, Gallery, Sustainability, Visit
- Mobile hamburger menu using front-end JavaScript only
- Smooth scrolling anchors
- Lazy-loading images using native loading="lazy" or IntersectionObserver
- Subtle animations on card reveal while scrolling
- Accessible contrast and readable typography
- Use simple icons or emoji-style small symbols if needed, but keep elegant
- Add footer with newsletter-looking section, but it should be static only, no email sending

10. Components / UI details
- Header / Navbar
- Hero section
- Horizontal card row component
- Menu card component
- Blog card component
- Sustainability stat card
- Gallery card
- Footer
- Static contact form component
- Article layout component

Content tone:
- Warm, poetic, personal, nature-loving
- Should sound like a real person writing a food and environment blog
- Avoid corporate startup feel
- Use realistic sample text, not lorem ipsum

Deliverable:
- Build a complete static front-end website that runs locally without any external services
- React is preferred, with plain CSS or CSS modules, no backend
- All data can be stored in local arrays / JSON files inside the project
- Do not add authentication, database, API calls, admin panel, live reservations, payment, or server-side code
- The final result should look polished, medium complexity, nature restaurant + personal environmental blog, with Netflix-inspired browsing rows and lazy-loaded visual cards.",
 "judge": {
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8",

  "request_model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8:novita",
  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
